name: SPX JEV questions, both lanes

generated_from.set: SPX JEV question set, final (round 3: audits applied)

status: generated by spec/write_question_docs.py: edit the set and regenerate, never this file
owner_rule: A question goes to shadow only once proven not to help JEV's direction call; unproven questions stay live and the learning loop's weights sort them out.
how_to_use: Step 2 of the pipeline. Each lane asks the questions whose lanes name it (the live lane thirty_minute, the opening lane opening_five_minute), at the reads its schedule names: live ones count in the sums, shadow ones are asked and logged but never summed, dark ones are never asked. A question with sleep_when is asked only when its label family says it is awake. Every threshold is a name in braces filled from spx_jev/cuts.py.

groups.purpose: Feed the 09:35-10:30 ten-minute five-way call: gap size, which side of the settled open wins, fresh session extremes, and how contested and busy the open is.

gap_size.cadence: once at the 09:35 read on the settled open; answer held as a day constant to 10:30 (code weights it by minutes since the open)
gap_size.ask: How large was this morning's gap from yesterday's close?
gap_size.instructions: Read `gap.size`. How large was this morning's gap between yesterday's close and the settled open, whichever way it went, against the recent sessions' gaps?
criteria: the gap was in the bottom third of the recent sessions' gaps
the gap was in the middle third of the recent sessions' gaps
the gap was in the top third of the recent sessions' gaps
code_criteria: |gap| larger than under a third of the prior sessions' |gap| (bottom third)
|gap| larger than a third to two thirds of them (middle third)
|gap| larger than over two thirds of them (top third)
gap_size.why: Gap size sets how busy the first half hour is; it says nothing about the next 10 minutes' direction, so it serves size only and is asked once instead of twelve identical times.

opening_side.cadence: every 5 min 09:45-10:30, from the first read with a live tape unit (code weights by minutes-since-open bucket; the 09:50-10:05 bucket carries the effect)
opening_side.ask: Which side of the settled open does the opening favour now?
opening_side.instructions: Read `open.path`. Where price is now, in tape units from the settled open, decides first. Check rotating first. Which side of the settled open does the opening favour now?

criteria.up_firm: now more than one tape unit above the open, and it has given back less than the stall line of its high
criteria.up_fading: now more than one tape unit above the open, but it has given back the stall line or more of its high
criteria.rotating: within one tape unit of the open now
criteria.down_fading: now more than one tape unit below the open, but it has given back the stall line or more of its low
criteria.down_firm: now more than one tape unit below the open, and it has given back less than the stall line of its low

code_criteria.down_fading: mirror of up_fading below the open
code_criteria.down_firm: mirror of up_firm below the open

opening_side.why: Replaces opening_drive's seven options with five signed ones: stalling and failed flipped sign between windows on 10-24 reads, and tested_then_reversed fired on 2 of 59 days.

fresh_extreme_5m.cadence: every 5 min 09:45-10:30 with a 5-minute window; then every 30-minute read with a 30-minute window
fresh_extreme_5m.ask: Did price just set a new session high or low, or stall near one?
fresh_extreme_5m.instructions: Read `open.fresh_extreme` and `price.day_range_position`. Over the window the label names, did price set a new high or low for the session, or is it sitting near one without setting a new one? Check in order: both_new, new_high, new_low, stalled_near_high, stalled_near_low, middle.

criteria.new_high: price set a new session high in the window and no new low
criteria.new_low: price set a new session low in the window and no new high
criteria.both_new: price set both a new high and a new low in the window
criteria.stalled_near_high: no new extreme in the window, and price sits in the top band of today's range
criteria.stalled_near_low: no new extreme in the window, and price sits in the bottom band of today's range
criteria.middle: no new extreme, and price sits between the top and bottom bands of today's range

code_criteria.new_high: max high of the window's bars > session high before them; no new low

fresh_extreme_5m.why: The one opening state with positive held-out skill on the lane's own grading; it folds the opening-range break in as a label clause because the break carries almost nothing once the fresh extreme is known.

open_contested.ask: How contested has the settled open been so far?
open_contested.instructions: Read `open.settled_open_crosses`. How contested is the settled open so far?

criteria.one_sided: price has stayed on one side of the settled open, crossing it no more than once
criteria.some_crossing: price has crossed the settled open more than once but fewer than {open_contested_crosses} times
criteria.contested: price has crossed the settled open {open_contested_crosses} or more times

open_contested.why: Repeated fights over the settled open mean two-way flow is active: the next 10 minutes run larger, even after a quiet 5 minutes, which moves weight out of the five-way flat bucket.

opening_pace.cadence: every 5 min 09:45-10:30 (asleep while the tape unit is held before 09:45)
opening_pace.ask: How busy is the opening for this time of day?
opening_pace.instructions: Read `tape.unit_vs_normal` and `range.today_vs_normal`. Check very_busy first. How busy is the opening right now for this time of day?
criteria: both narrow for this time of day, or one narrow and one ordinary
both ordinary for this time of day, or one wide and one narrow
one wide and the other ordinary
both wide, or the tape unit wider than any recent session
code_criteria: both bottom third, or one bottom one middle
both middle, or one top one bottom
both top third, or the wider-than-all flag
opening_pace.why: The median of three 5-minute ranges is the lane's own outcome unit and forecasts the next 10 minutes better than the last 5 minutes, which also carries the stale 09:30 catch-up.

groups.purpose: The non-price opening reads: net volume, TICK (average and bursts), large 0DTE prints and premium bursts, the call-put swing of new 0DTE volume, the same-day put tilt against the clock, and chips/financials tells.

open_net_volume_lean.ask: Since the open, has net volume leaned to buying or selling against a usual morning?
open_net_volume_lean.instructions: Read `breadth.open_net_volume`. Since the open, compared with a usual morning at this minute, has net volume leaned to buying, to selling, or split between NYSE-wide and S&P 500 stocks?

criteria.both_buying: NYSE and S&P 500 net volume are both more than {open_vol_z} of their usual swing to the buy side
criteria.both_selling: both more than {open_vol_z} of their usual swing to the sell side
criteria.split: one leans past {open_vol_z} one way and the other does not lean the same way
criteria.no_lean: both are within {open_vol_z} of their usual swing

code_criteria.split: exactly one past the cut, or opposite signs past it

open_net_volume_lean.why: The only opening input in review whose interval clears zero and holds after removing the price move; it is the 10-minute breadth read round 1 asked for, with the advance-decline thrust folded in.

opening_tick_lean.ask: Since the open, how one-sided has market-wide buying and selling been?
opening_tick_lean.instructions: Read `breadth.opening_tick`. Since the open, how one-sided has market-wide buying and selling been?

criteria.one_sided_buying: TICK highs reached the top burst band for these minutes {open_cluster_min} or more times and its lows never reached the bottom band
criteria.leaning_buying: TICK averaged on the buy side without a buying cluster
criteria.two_way_open: TICK averaged near zero, or burst both ways
criteria.leaning_selling: TICK averaged on the sell side without a selling cluster
criteria.one_sided_selling: TICK lows reached the bottom burst band {open_cluster_min} or more times and its highs never reached the top band

code_criteria.one_sided_buying: bursts >= {open_cluster_min} above the same-minute {tick_burst_pct} percentile of bar highs, none below the mirror

opening_tick_lean.why: Traders read opening TICK clusters as trend-day tells; the fixed plus-or-minus-1000 line may never fire on SPX (probe closes -829..+944), so the burst band is a same-minute percentile of bar highs and lows.

big_print_lean_open.ask: Which way did the large same-day option trades of the last {window_10_min} minutes lean?
big_print_lean_open.instructions: Read `options.big_prints_10`. Over the last {window_10_min} minutes, did large single same-day option trades happen, and which way did they lean?

criteria.bullish_lean: large trades put more than {big_lean_share} of premium on calls bought or puts sold
criteria.bearish_lean: large trades put more than {big_lean_share} of premium on puts bought or calls sold
criteria.mixed: large trades happened but neither side reached {big_lean_share}

code_criteria.bullish_lean: prints >= {big_print_lots} lots, count >= {big_min_prints}, bullish premium share > {big_lean_share}

big_print_lean_open.why: The only opening flow read with a measured sign (contrarian); it reads single large trades, not the whole tape, which is why the aggressor-lean shadow result does not settle it.

zero_dte_side_shift_open.ask: Did new same-day option volume in the last {window_10_min} minutes shift to calls or to puts?
zero_dte_side_shift_open.instructions: Read `options.call_put_shift_10m`. Over the last {window_10_min} minutes, did new same-day option volume lean clearly to calls or to puts compared with the day so far?

criteria.shift_to_calls: new volume's call share beat the day's call share by more than {call_put_shift_share}
criteria.shift_to_puts: new volume's put share beat the day's put share by more than {call_put_shift_share}
criteria.no_shift: the split stayed within {call_put_shift_share} of the day's split
criteria.too_thin: too little new volume to judge

code_criteria.shift_to_calls: call share last window - call share since open > {call_put_shift_share}
code_criteria.too_thin: new contracts below the same-clock {thin_volume_pct} percentile

zero_dte_side_shift_open.why: 0DTE is about half of SPX option volume and the opening flow is where it shows first; the sign (hedging vs chasing) is unknown, so code learns it.

put_tilt_vs_clock.sleep_when: fewer than {min_rank_sessions} prior sessions at this minute, or a needed option price missing (label omitted)
put_tilt_vs_clock.ask: How steeply are same-day puts priced over calls against recent sessions at this minute?
put_tilt_vs_clock.instructions: Read `skew.put_tilt_vs_usual`. Compared with the same minute on recent sessions, how steeply are same-day puts priced over same-day calls right now? Check call_tilt first; then the rank words decide.

criteria.steep_put_tilt: puts priced over calls more steeply than on most recent sessions at this minute, past the steep rank
criteria.usual_tilt: the tilt is within the usual range for this minute
criteria.flat_tilt: puts priced over calls less steeply than usual, past the flat rank, but still above calls
criteria.call_tilt: same-day calls are priced above same-day puts at equal distance

code_criteria.steep_put_tilt: tilt rank >= {skew_steep_rank} vs the prior sessions at the same minute
code_criteria.flat_tilt: rank <= {skew_flat_rank} and put-call gap is zero or positive
code_criteria.call_tilt: put IV minus call IV at equal distance is negative (checked first)

put_tilt_vs_clock.why: Skew was not missing from history after all: the tape's quotes rebuild it. Raw skew is the clock (it decays from 0.15 to 0.03 through the day), so only the clock rank is asked; the far-put wing rides as a clause.

opening_tells_10m.ask: Did semiconductors or financials break away from the index in the last {window_10_min} minutes?
opening_tells_10m.instructions: Read `tells.sector_lead_10m`. Over the last {window_10_min} minutes, after scaling for how much each normally moves, did semiconductors or financials break away from the index, and which way?

criteria.both_up: semis and financials both ran ahead upward by a top-fifth margin for this time
criteria.both_down: both ran ahead downward by a top-fifth margin
criteria.financials_only: only financials broke away, either way (a rates tell)
criteria.split: one broke away up and the other down
criteria.in_line: neither broke away by a top-fifth margin

opening_tells_10m.why: Chips lead the AI-weighted index at the open; splitting the semis option by side lets the loop learn direction without the side hiding in the label.

opening_premium_burst.cadence: every 5 min 09:40-10:30, awake only when the last 5 minutes' 0DTE premium is in the top fifth for these minutes
opening_premium_burst.ask: Which way did the burst of same-day option premium lean?
opening_premium_burst.instructions: Read `options.premium_burst_5m`. A burst of same-day option premium just traded. Which way did it lean?

criteria.burst_bullish: more than {big_lean_share} of the burst's premium was calls bought or puts sold
criteria.burst_bearish: more than {big_lean_share} of the burst's premium was puts bought or calls sold

opening_premium_burst.why: A premium burst in the first hour is the tape's loudest opening flow read; round 1 cut it only to keep a request at six.

tick_extreme_follow.cadence: every 5 min 09:40-10:30, awake only when a TICK burst printed in the last 5 minutes
tick_extreme_follow.sleep_when: no TICK burst in the last 5 minutes
tick_extreme_follow.ask: Did SPX follow the NYSE TICK's burst to an extreme?
tick_extreme_follow.instructions: Read `breadth.tick_extreme_5m`. NYSE TICK just burst to an extreme for this minute. Did SPX follow it over the same five minutes? Check both_ways first.

criteria.buy_burst_followed: a buying burst, and SPX rose past the follow line
criteria.buy_burst_stalled: a buying burst, and SPX did not rise past the follow line
criteria.sell_burst_followed: a selling burst, and SPX fell past the follow line
criteria.sell_burst_stalled: a selling burst, and SPX did not fall past the follow line
criteria.both_ways: bursts both ways in the same five minutes

code_criteria.both_ways: high above the {tick_burst_pct} band and low below the mirror band (checked first)
code_criteria.buy_burst_followed: high burst only, SPX five-minute move > +{tick_follow_sigma}

tick_extreme_follow.why: Round 1 named a five-minute TICK-extreme read as the opening lane's round-2 candidate; a burst the index does not follow is the classic absorption tell.

groups.purpose: Day constants asked once at the 09:35 read and held: the heavyweight gap split, the open against yesterday's range, VIX's first print against the gap, and the morning brief against the gap.

heavyweight_gap_split.cadence: once at the 09:35 read on the settled open; answer held as a day constant through the lane and the 30-minute reads to 11:32
heavyweight_gap_split.ask: Did the rest of the index gap the same way as the heavyweight that moved it?
heavyweight_gap_split.instructions: Read `leaders.heavyweight_gap`. One of the largest index stocks moved the index past the shock rule between yesterday's close and the settled open. Did the rest of the index gap the same way, the other way, or barely move?

criteria.shock_up_rest_up: one heavyweight lifted the index past the shock rule and the rest of the index also gapped up
criteria.shock_down_rest_down: one heavyweight dragged the index past the shock rule and the rest also gapped down
criteria.shock_up_rest_down: one heavyweight lifted the index past the shock rule while the rest gapped down
criteria.shock_down_rest_up: one heavyweight dragged the index past the shock rule while the rest gapped up
criteria.shock_rest_flat: one heavyweight moved the index past the shock rule and the rest barely moved

heavyweight_gap_split.why: When one stock is the index, SPX's gap is not the market's gap; on earnings reaction days the reporter's gap held and drifted instead of fading, which gap_origin used to mislabel as thin overnight drift.

open_vs_prior_range.cadence: once at the 09:35 read; answer held as a day constant through the lane and the 30-minute reads to 11:32
open_vs_prior_range.ask: Where did the open land against yesterday's high and low?
open_vs_prior_range.instructions: Read `levels.open_vs_prior_range`. Where is the open against yesterday's high and low?

criteria.above_prior_high: opened more than the buffer above yesterday's high
criteria.upper_inside: inside, or within the buffer of, yesterday's high: upper half of yesterday's range
criteria.lower_inside: inside, or within the buffer of, yesterday's low: lower half of yesterday's range
criteria.below_prior_low: opened more than the buffer below yesterday's low

code_criteria.upper_inside: open above the midpoint and <= prior high + {outside_buffer_sigma}
code_criteria.lower_inside: open below the midpoint and >= prior low - {outside_buffer_sigma}

open_vs_prior_range.why: An open outside yesterday's whole range meets no overhead or underfoot trade from the day before; it is a stronger vote than the gap alone and sets up a bigger morning.

vix_overnight_surprise.cadence: once at the 09:35 read; answer held as a day constant through the lane and the 30-minute reads to 11:32
vix_overnight_surprise.ask: Did VIX open higher, in line or lower than the overnight gap would leave it?
vix_overnight_surprise.instructions: Read `vol.vix_overnight_surprise`. Is VIX's first print today higher, in line, or lower than the overnight gap would normally leave it?

criteria.fear_rich: VIX opened more than the surprise line above what the gap implies
criteria.in_line: within the surprise line of what the gap implies
criteria.fear_cheap: VIX opened more than the surprise line below what the gap implies

vix_overnight_surprise.why: Raw overnight VIX just repeats the gap (corr -0.79); what is new is hedging demand beyond the price move, and it leans contrarian.

brief_vs_tape.cadence: once at the 09:35 read; answer held as a day constant through the lane and the 30-minute reads to 11:32
brief_vs_tape.ask: What does the morning news brief add to this morning's gap?
brief_vs_tape.instructions: Read `news.morning_brief`. Check no_view first. Compared with this morning's gap, what does the morning news brief add?

criteria.no_view: the brief barely leans or has low confidence
criteria.restates: the brief leans the same way as a gap past the gap rule
criteria.leans_against: the brief leans the opposite way to a gap past the gap rule
criteria.leans_without_move: the brief takes a side while the gap is inside the gap rule

brief_vs_tape.why: The brief is the only news read the station makes, but it mostly repeats the futures; asking what it adds keeps it from double-counting the gap. Only leans_against can add anything.

groups.purpose: The single carrier of the move's sign plus how the move was made: with or against the day, burst/choppy/clean, one-way hours, wide chop under a flat net move, and the day's character.

price_move_5way.ask: Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, how did price move?
price_move_5way.instructions: Read `price.recent_move`. Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, which describes price?
criteria: price fell more than {move_strong_sigma} sigma
price fell between {move_rule_sigma} and {move_strong_sigma} sigma
price moved less than {move_rule_sigma} sigma either way
price rose between {move_rule_sigma} and {move_strong_sigma} sigma
price rose more than {move_strong_sigma} sigma
price_move_5way.why: The single carrier of the move's sign for code to cross with other answers (so it serves direction); code also folds the options into |move| tiers for the size book, where the strong tier sharpens the flat call. It is also the reading canary: its answer key is the label's own band.

leg_vs_day_side.cadence: every 30-minute read 10:02-14:32 (sign flips into the close)
leg_vs_day_side.ask: Did the latest leg run with or against the day's side of yesterday's close?
leg_vs_day_side.instructions: Read `price.recent_move` for the last {window_30_min} minutes and `price.vs_prior_close` for where SPX sits against yesterday's close. Check quiet first. Which describes the latest leg?

criteria.quiet: the last half hour moved less than the move rule, and the day is near yesterday's close
criteria.quiet_leg_day_moved: the last half hour moved less than the move rule, but the day is well away from yesterday's close
criteria.leg_with_day: the last half hour moved past the move rule in the same direction as the day's move from yesterday's close
criteria.leg_against_day: the last half hour moved past the move rule against the day's move from yesterday's close
criteria.leg_on_flat_day: the last half hour moved past the move rule, but the day is near yesterday's close

leg_vs_day_side.why: The 30-minute move alone predicts almost nothing; split by the day's side measured from yesterday's close, legs with the day tend to continue and legs against it tend to fade.

move_shape.ask: How was the last half hour's move made?
move_shape.instructions: Read `price.recent_move` and `price.move_shape`. Check no_move first, then burst, then choppy. How was the last half hour's move made?

criteria.no_move: price moved less than the move rule
criteria.burst: one five-minute stretch made most of the move
criteria.choppy: price covered a lot of ground but kept doubling back, ending with a small share of it as net move
criteria.clean: the move was spread across the half hour and went mostly one way

code_criteria.burst: largest five-minute chunk >= {move_burst_share} of the net move

move_shape.why: Burst and choppy moves both leave price unsettled and bigger moves follow; clean moves continued before mid-afternoon and faded after, a clock interaction code weights by phase. The engine already computes path efficiency; no round-1 question read it.

one_way_hour.ask: Was the last {window_60_min} minutes one-way or two-way?
one_way_hour.instructions: Read `price.hour_one_way`. Which describes the last {window_60_min} minutes?

criteria.one_way_up: price rose past the one-way size and barely came back through its own hourly average
criteria.one_way_down: price fell past the one-way size and barely came back through its own hourly average
criteria.two_way_up: price rose past the one-way size but traded back and forth through its hourly average
criteria.two_way_down: price fell past the one-way size but traded back and forth through its hourly average
criteria.no_hour_move: the hour's net move was under the one-way size

one_way_hour.why: An hour that moved one way without trading back through its own average has used up its one-sided flow and tends to give some back; the only chop measure that carried direction.

hour_range_vs_net.ask: Did the last half hour move, and was its range narrow or wide?
hour_range_vs_net.instructions: Read `range.hour_vs_clock` and `price.recent_move`. Decide first whether the last half hour moved past the move rule. Which situation is it?

criteria.quiet_narrow: the last half hour barely moved and the last hour's range is narrow or ordinary for this time of day
criteria.wide_chop: the last half hour barely moved net, but the last hour's range is wide for this time of day
criteria.moved_narrow: the last half hour moved past the rule inside a narrow or ordinary hour range
criteria.moved_wide: the last half hour moved past the rule and the hour's range is wide for this time of day

hour_range_vs_net.why: A flat net move hides a wide two-way hour; that state is flat far less often and carries more than double the both-ways whipsaw risk, so it pushes P(flat) down and tells code to trust direction less.

day_character.ask: So far today, are the moves building or cancelling out?
day_character.instructions: Read `price.day_character`. So far today, have half-hour stretches been larger, similar or smaller than their five-minute pieces would suggest?

criteria.moves_building: half-hour stretches have been larger than their five-minute pieces suggest
criteria.mixed: about what the five-minute pieces suggest
criteria.moves_cancelling: half-hour stretches have been smaller than their five-minute pieces suggest

day_character.why: A description of the day so far, not a forecast: the old 'trending / mean_reverting' names invited a continuation call the data contradicts, so the options now describe the past and code learns the sign.

groups.purpose: The gap's fate from 10:00 to mid-afternoon (signed), whether a faded gap reasserts after noon, the day's side measured from yesterday's close, the first-hour break and the noise band.

gap_side_now.ask: Is this morning's gap intact or being lost?
gap_side_now.instructions: Read `gap.size` and `gap.fill_progress`. Where price sits now decides first; the history second. Which describes the gap now?

criteria.gap_up_intact: opened more than {gap_rule_sigma} sigma above yesterday's close, still keeps the half line or more of that gap, and has not touched yesterday's close
criteria.gap_up_losing: opened more than {gap_rule_sigma} sigma above and now keeps less than the half line of it, or has touched yesterday's close
criteria.no_gap: opened within {gap_rule_sigma} sigma of yesterday's close
criteria.gap_down_losing: opened more than {gap_rule_sigma} sigma below and now keeps less than the half line of it, or has touched yesterday's close
criteria.gap_down_intact: opened more than {gap_rule_sigma} sigma below yesterday's close, still keeps the half line or more of that gap, and has not touched yesterday's close

gap_side_now.why: Replaces gap_fill_state's unsigned options: 'holding' mixed gap-up and gap-down days, so the loop learned the summer's gap mix instead of the rule. Signed options each hold 15-35% of days, and the location-first wording follows the SNDK back-inside fix.

gap_fill_next_hour.cadence: every 30-minute read, awake only while code's answer key for gap_side_now is gap_up_losing or gap_down_losing (never JEV's own answer, which would be circular)
gap_fill_next_hour.sleep_when: code's answer key for gap_side_now is not gap_up_losing / gap_down_losing
gap_fill_next_hour.ask: Will price trade back to yesterday's close within the next {window_60_min} minutes?
gap_fill_next_hour.instructions: Read `gap.size`, `gap.fill_progress` and `gap.reach_distance`. Within the next {window_60_min} minutes, does price trade at or through yesterday's close?

criteria.true: price trades at or through yesterday's close within the window
criteria.false: price does not reach yesterday's close within the window

code_criteria.true: graded offline: a bar touches prior_close within {gap_touch_sigma} sigma

gap_fill_next_hour.why: A directly gradable forecast that feeds P(flat); asked only where it is uncertain.

gap_reasserts.cadence: every 30-minute read 11:32-14:32, awake only on real-gap days
gap_reasserts.ask: From the settled open to late morning, did price go with the gap or fill it?
gap_reasserts.instructions: Read `gap.size` and `gap.morning_vs_gap`. From the settled open to the late morning, did price go with this morning's gap or against it, and did it touch yesterday's close?

criteria.morning_with_gap: between the settled open and the late morning, price moved further the gap's way
criteria.morning_faded_unfilled: price moved against the gap by the late morning but never touched yesterday's close
criteria.morning_filled: price moved against the gap and touched yesterday's close by the late morning

code_criteria.morning_faded_unfilled: opposite sign, no touch of prior_close

gap_reasserts.why: Overnight gaps get pulled back early, then the direction the overnight market voted for often comes back after noon; the side lives in the label and code applies it.

day_side_from_close.cadence: every 30-minute read 10:02-14:32 (not after: the sign flips into the close)
day_side_from_close.ask: Is SPX's move from yesterday's close from the gap or built today?
day_side_from_close.instructions: Read `price.day_move_split` for how far SPX sits from yesterday's close and how much of that came from the opening gap versus trading since the open. Check near_close first.

criteria.near_close: price is within {day_side_sigma} sigma of yesterday's close
criteria.up_on_gap: more than {day_side_sigma} sigma above yesterday's close, and most of it came from the opening gap
criteria.up_built_today: more than {day_side_sigma} sigma above yesterday's close, and most of it came from trading since the open
criteria.down_on_gap: more than {day_side_sigma} sigma below yesterday's close, and most of it came from the opening gap
criteria.down_built_today: more than {day_side_sigma} sigma below yesterday's close, and most of it came from trading since the open

code_criteria.up_on_gap: above by more than {day_side_sigma} and gap share >= {gap_half_share}, same sign
code_criteria.up_built_today: above by more than {day_side_sigma} and gap share < {gap_half_share} or opposite sign

day_side_from_close.why: Round 1 measured the day only from the settled open, which carries no momentum on SPX; the move from yesterday's close does carry forward through midday, and the gap is the part that carries it.

first_hour_break_side.ask: What has price done with the first hour's range since?
first_hour_break_side.instructions: Read `range.first_hour`. Since the first hour ended, what has price done with its range? Where price is now decides; a price back inside counts as back inside.

criteria.inside: neither edge broken since the first hour ended
criteria.extending: one edge broken, price still beyond it, and it reached the extension line past it
criteria.stalling: one edge broken, price still beyond it, not yet at the extension line
criteria.failed: one edge broken, price now back inside

code_criteria.inside: no bar more than {ib_break_sigma} beyond either edge

first_hour_break_side.why: Ten options folded to five: each mirrored pair shared one effect across two thin cells, and the loop learns direction relative to the broken edge's side (still_forming is replaced by sleeping before the first hour ends).

open_noise_band.ask: Where is price against the usual move-from-the-open band for this minute?
open_noise_band.instructions: Read `open.noise_band`. Where is price against the usual move-from-the-open band for this minute? Check at_an_edge before above or below.

criteria.at_an_edge: price is within {noise_edge_sigma} sigma of either edge
criteria.above_band: more than {noise_edge_sigma} sigma above the upper edge
criteria.below_band: more than {noise_edge_sigma} sigma below the lower edge
criteria.inside_band: well inside the usual band for this time of day

open_noise_band.why: A trend-versus-noise read anchored at the higher and lower of the open and yesterday's close, averaged over the prior 14 sessions; kept as a regime read, not as the source strategy's Sharpe.

prior_close_push_fade.cadence: the 14:32 and 15:02 reads, awake only when the last half hour moved toward yesterday's close past the move rule and price is within the push distance of it or crossed it in the window
prior_close_push_fade.sleep_when: last-30 move not toward prior_close past {move_rule_sigma}, or price beyond {close_push_sigma} of it without a cross
prior_close_push_fade.ref_side: side of yesterday's close price started from
prior_close_push_fade.ask: Where does the late push stand against yesterday's close?
prior_close_push_fade.instructions: Read `price.prior_close_push`. Price has pushed toward yesterday's close late in the day. Where does it stand against that close now?

criteria.crossed_through: price crossed yesterday's close within the last half hour and is still through it
criteria.crossed_back: price crossed yesterday's close within the last half hour but is back on its starting side
criteria.pressing_short: price has not crossed yesterday's close and sits within the push distance of it

code_criteria.crossed_through: crossed prior_close within {window_30_min} min, now on the far side
code_criteria.crossed_back: crossed within {window_30_min} min, now back on the starting side

prior_close_push_fade.why: Yesterday's close is the level every desk marks into the close; a late push that stalls short of it or crosses and fails is a fade setup, and one that holds through it is a flip of the day's sign.

groups.purpose: How big the next half hour will be: realized swing vs the clock, the straddle vs the clock, VIX stir, how hard the flat band is to hit, day energy and SPY's quote.

realized_vs_clock.ask: How busy was the last half hour against the same half hour on recent sessions?
realized_vs_clock.instructions: Read `vol.realized_vs_clock`. How busy was the last half hour compared with the same half hour on recent sessions? Check coiled first.

criteria.coiled: bottom fifth for this half hour and no real move for at least the last half hour
criteria.quiet: bottom fifth for this half hour, with a real move ending inside the last half hour
criteria.ordinary: between the bottom and top fifth
criteria.busy: top fifth, not wider than every recent session
criteria.very_busy: wider than every recent session at this time of day

code_criteria.coiled: rank <= {bottom_fifth} and time since last move >= {window_30_min}

realized_vs_clock.why: Recent realized movement is the best single forecaster of the next half hour's size; ranking it at the same clock removes the U-shape. Dividing by the straddle (round 1) cancelled most of that information, and coil_state's fixed cuts were the clock (coiled 0% at 10:00, 37% at 14:00).

straddle_vs_clock.ask: Is the rest of today priced cheaper or richer than usual for this time of day?
straddle_vs_clock.instructions: Read `vol.straddle_vs_clock`. Compared with a normal session at this time of day, is the options market pricing the rest of today cheaper than usual, about usual, or richer than usual?
criteria: the straddle left is under {straddle_cheap} times its usual share of the opening straddle
{straddle_cheap} to {straddle_rich} times its usual share
over {straddle_rich} times its usual share
straddle_vs_clock.why: The one home for the live straddle and the 0DTE vol pop (sigma_live over anchor correlates 0.87 with this ratio); it absorbs today_vs_month's proxy form, and a one-day VIX clause joins once that series has a same-clock baseline.

vix_stir.cadence: every 5 min 09:40-10:30 with a 10-minute window; every 30-minute read from 10:02 with a 30-minute window (the 10:02 read measures VIX since the open)
vix_stir.ask: How much has VIX moved as a share of its level?
vix_stir.instructions: Read `vol.vix_change_30`. Over the window the label names, how much has VIX moved, in either direction, as a share of its level? The label's line words decide.
criteria: under the still line for the window
between the still line and the moving line
between the moving line and the jump line
past the jump line
vix_stir.why: A VIX move adds to next-move size beyond the SPX move; fixed points break as VIX rises ('jumping' was 2.6% of reads on lower-VIX days vs 15.6% on higher), so the bands are a share of the level. vix_open_path folds in: its four-way split added nothing at 10 minutes.

flat_band_reach.horizon: 30min (asked once a read; the label's 60-minute clause is not this question's)
flat_band_reach.ask: How wide is the flat band against SPX's typical move over the horizon?
flat_band_reach.instructions: Read `ruler.flat_band_reach`. Is the next-30-minute flat band narrow, middling or wide compared with how far SPX typically moves over the next 30 minutes right now? The first clause, the 30-minute one, decides; the 60-minute clause after it does not.
criteria: the flat band covers under the narrow share of a typical 30-minute move: price usually travels past it
between the narrow and wide shares
more than the wide share of a typical 30-minute move: price usually stays inside it
flat_band_reach.why: The flat leg is most of the up/flat/down score; the clock knows the hour but not whether today is quiet. One number tells JEV how hard 'flat' is to hit.

spx_range_pace.ask: How does today's range so far compare with a normal day's pace?
spx_range_pace.instructions: Read `range.pace_vs_priced`. The label's band words decide. Today's range so far, measured against a one-sigma move for the time elapsed, is it under, near, over or far over that line?
criteria: under {range_pace_sleepy} of a one-sigma move for the time elapsed
{range_pace_sleepy} to {one_ratio}
{one_ratio} to {range_pace_wild}
more than {range_pace_wild}
spx_range_pace.why: Day energy. The denominator is a one-sigma move from the morning ruler, not 'the range the options market priced' (the ruler overstates realized about 2.5x), so the label says what it measures.

spy_liquidity.ask: Is SPY's quote wider or thinner than usual for this time of day?
spy_liquidity.instructions: Read `liquidity.spy_quote`. Is SPY's quote wide or its displayed size thin compared with its usual for this time of day?

criteria.wide_spread: SPY's quoted spread has been wider than its usual, at or past the wide line
criteria.thin_book: the spread is usual but the size showing at SPY's best prices is in the bottom fifth for this time
criteria.tight_spread: the spread has been at its tightest tick

spy_liquidity.why: The only equity liquidity read: a wide quote on the most liquid ETF means market makers are pulling back, which comes before bigger swings, clearest in the afternoon. It says nothing about direction.

straddle_repricing.ask: Did the last {window_30_min} minutes reprice the rest of today richer or cheaper than the clock?
straddle_repricing.instructions: Read `vol.straddle_reprice_30`. Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, did the options market reprice the rest of today richer or cheaper than the clock alone would have left it?
criteria: the straddle ended cheaper than the clock alone would leave it by more than the repricing line
within the repricing line of what the clock alone would leave
the straddle ended richer than the clock alone would leave it by more than the repricing line
straddle_repricing.why: The straddle's level is straddle_vs_clock; its change against pure time decay is the market repricing the afternoon, a size read the level hides.

average_reach_30.cadence: every 30-minute read from 10:32, awake only while price is more than the move rule from the day's average price
average_reach_30.ask: Will price trade at the day's volume-weighted average within the next {window_30_min} minutes?
average_reach_30.instructions: Read `price.vs_vwap` and `price.vwap_reach`. Within the next {window_30_min} minutes, does price trade at the day's volume-weighted average price?

criteria.true: price trades at the day's average within the window
criteria.false: price does not reach the day's average within the window

code_criteria.true: graded offline: a bar's range spans vwap within {vwap_touch_sigma} sigma

average_reach_30.why: A directly gradable reach forecast for the flat bucket: the day's average is the level most intraday flow trades back to.

groups.purpose: Vol moving beyond what price explains: VIX, VVIX, the VVIX pairing with the move, the VIX9D shift, same-day skew and at-the-money IV.

vix_vs_price.ask: Did VIX move more or less fearfully than the SPX move explains?
vix_vs_price.instructions: Read `vol.vix_vs_price`. Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, did VIX move more fearfully than the SPX move alone explains, less fearfully, or in line? The opening words decide.

criteria.fear_ahead_of_price: VIX rose more than the residual line above what the SPX move explains
criteria.in_line: within the residual line of what the SPX move explains
criteria.calm_ahead_of_price: VIX fell more than the residual line below what the SPX move explains

vix_vs_price.why: Fear showing up in VIX before price is how an unscheduled headline often appears first. Size is the stable part; the direction lean is unstable, so the why no longer calls it the best direction candidate and code learns any sign.

vvix_hidden_stir.ask: Did VVIX stir beyond what the VIX and SPX moves explain?
vvix_hidden_stir.instructions: Read `vol.vvix_vs_vix`. Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, how much did VVIX move beyond what the VIX move and the SPX move explain, either direction?

criteria.still: leftover VVIX move below the median of recent reads
criteria.stirring: leftover move between the median and the top fifth of recent reads
criteria.churning: leftover move in the top fifth of recent reads, while SPX or VIX also moved
criteria.churning_while_quiet: leftover move in the top fifth while SPX and VIX themselves barely moved

vvix_hidden_stir.why: Raw VVIX mostly repeats VIX (corr 0.74-0.76); the leftover flags hedging in the VIX options market that neither price nor VIX shows yet, often the first sign a pinned afternoon is about to break.

spot_vvix_pairing.ask: Did SPX move, and did VVIX rise or fall with it?
spot_vvix_pairing.instructions: Read `vol.vvix_with_move`. Do not say which way SPX went. Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, did SPX move past the pairing rule, and did VVIX rise or fall with that move?

criteria.move_vvix_up: SPX moved past the pairing rule and VVIX rose
criteria.move_vvix_down: SPX moved past the pairing rule and VVIX fell or held
criteria.no_move: SPX moved less than the pairing rule

code_criteria.move_vvix_up: |SPX half-hour move| > {pair_move_sigma} and VVIX change positive
code_criteria.move_vvix_down: |SPX half-hour move| > {pair_move_sigma} and VVIX change zero or negative

spot_vvix_pairing.why: VIX nearly always rises on a drop, but VVIX rising or falling separates a panicked selloff (bounces) from an orderly one (continues), and flags unstable rallies. Replaces the deferred spot_vix_pairing.

front_fear_shift.ask: Did nine-day fear rise or fall against the VIX?
front_fear_shift.instructions: Read `vol.front_fear_shift`. Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, did nine-day fear rise against the VIX, fall against it, or hold? The opening words decide.

criteria.front_rising: nine-day VIX gained more than the shift rule on VIX
criteria.holding: the gap between nine-day VIX and VIX moved less than the shift rule
criteria.front_falling: nine-day VIX lost more than the shift rule against VIX

front_fear_shift.why: VIX9D's own change repeats VIX (corr 0.93) and the level gap is constant within the day; the shift in the gap is the only new intraday piece.

skew_vs_price.ask: Did downside protection get dearer or cheaper than the SPX move explains?
skew_vs_price.instructions: Read `skew.shift_vs_price`. Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, did same-day downside protection get dearer compared with upside bets by more than the SPX move alone explains, cheaper, or in line?

criteria.puts_bid_up: the put-over-call premium rose more than the skew line beyond what the SPX move explains
criteria.in_line: within the skew line of what the SPX move explains
criteria.puts_offered: the put-over-call premium fell more than the skew line below what the SPX move explains

skew_vs_price.why: Traders read 'puts getting bid' as a warning; only the part price does not explain is new. It is independent of the VIX residual (corr -0.007) and leans the other way, so the two must never be blended into one 'fear' sentence.

atm_iv_vs_price.ask: Did same-day at-the-money vol move more or less than the price move explains?
atm_iv_vs_price.instructions: Read `vol.atm_iv_residual`. Did same-day at-the-money vol move more or less than the price move explains?
criteria: vol rose more than the residual line beyond what price explains
vol moved within the residual line of what price explains
vol fell more than the residual line below what price explains
atm_iv_vs_price.why: The 0DTE version of vix_vs_price at the hour horizon showed a clean size effect in the opposite direction: an IV bid beyond price came before calmer trading.

groups.purpose: Scheduled events and the ruler's regime: the event clock (with pre-open, 10:00 and Fed-speaker tiers), the event cycle, releases inside the lane, the loaded ruler, the vol curve and stress state.

event_clock.cadence: every 30-minute read from 10:02; in the opening lane once at 09:35 and held (release_in_lane carries the 10-minute clock)
event_clock.sleep_when: no scheduled event today, or every event came out beyond the digest window
event_clock.ask: Where does this moment sit against today's scheduled events?
event_clock.instructions: Read `context.event_clock`. Where does this moment sit against today's scheduled events? The first match in this order wins: due_or_under_way, released_recently, fed_speaker_window, event_later_today, released_before_open.

criteria.due_or_under_way: a major release or its follow-on is due within the due window or under way
criteria.released_recently: an in-session release or Fed remarks came out within the digest window
criteria.fed_speaker_window: a scheduled Fed official is speaking now or is due within the speaker window
criteria.event_later_today: a major event is still to come today, beyond the due window
criteria.released_before_open: today's major report came before the open and nothing major remains in session

code_criteria.due_or_under_way: major start <= now + {event_due_min} or start <= now < end
code_criteria.fed_speaker_window: fed_speaker row start <= now + {speaker_window_min} and not ended
code_criteria.released_before_open: pre_open row today, nothing in session

event_clock.why: Code needs the phase. released_before_open could never fire (the calendar left out pre-open releases); the calendar now carries pre-open, 10:00 and Fed-speaker tiers, and the Fed-speaker window is the one scheduled slice of the dark news gap.

event_cycle_day.ask: Where does today sit in the cycle of major scheduled releases?
event_cycle_day.instructions: Read `calendar.event_cycle`. Where does today sit in the cycle of major scheduled releases (jobs, consumer prices, the Fed decision)? The first match in the order listed wins.

criteria.eve_of_fed: the Fed's rate decision is tomorrow
criteria.eve_of_jobs_or_cpi: the jobs report or the consumer price report comes out before tomorrow's open
criteria.day_after_event: yesterday was a major release day

code_criteria.eve_of_jobs_or_cpi: next session has JOBS or CPI pre-open
code_criteria.day_after_event: previous session had JOBS, CPI or FOMC

event_cycle_day.why: Eve afternoons trade at about a quarter of normal size and post-release sessions were among the narrowest on file; the clock and sigma cannot see tomorrow's calendar. The post_release_calm forecast folds in here.

release_in_lane.cadence: every 5 min 09:35-10:30, awake only when a release or speaker falls in the window
release_in_lane.sleep_when: nothing scheduled due within {window_10_min} minutes or started within the last {window_10_min}
release_in_lane.ask: Which scheduled release or Fed speaker falls inside this window?
release_in_lane.instructions: Read `event.release_clock_10m`. A scheduled release or Fed speaker is inside this window. Check in order: just_out, data_due_inside, speaker_due_inside.

criteria.data_due_inside: a mid-morning economic release is due inside the next window
criteria.speaker_due_inside: a scheduled Fed official's remarks start inside the next window
criteria.just_out: a release or speech started in the last window

release_in_lane.why: The lane's 10-minute size call sits across 10:00 on about a quarter of mornings; the window straddling a release is twice as big and the slots around it are not.

ruler_loaded.ask: Is today's priced move swollen or compressed, and is an event behind it?
ruler_loaded.instructions: Read `vol.ruler_event_load` with `context.event_clock`. Check in order: released_after_event, loaded_before_event, swollen_no_event, compressed, normal. Is today's options-priced move swollen by an event still to come, just released by an event that happened, swollen with no event, compressed, or normal?

criteria.loaded_before_event: the straddle prices far more than the tape delivers, more than usual for this minute, and a major event is still ahead today
criteria.released_after_event: a major event came out within the digest window and the tape is now moving more than the straddle priced beforehand
criteria.swollen_no_event: the morning ruler is at least the high line times its recent normal with no scheduled event
criteria.compressed: the morning ruler is at or under the low line times its recent normal

code_criteria.loaded_before_event: straddle-priced over tape-delivered half-hour move >= {loaded_ratio} and above its same-clock {top_fifth} rank, event ahead
code_criteria.released_after_event: event within {event_digest_min}, tape now moves more than the pre-event straddle priced

ruler_loaded.why: On event days every sigma and straddle label under-reads moves before the release and over-reads after; before the release the tape is not swollen, the ruler is. Code can use the answer to trust or rescale the size answers.

thirty_minute.then: re-asked only when code sees the answer change (checked every 30 minutes)

vol_curve_vs_usual.cadence: the 10:02 read, then only when the answer changes
vol_curve_vs_usual.ask: How is the VIX curve shaped against its usual?
vol_curve_vs_usual.instructions: Read `vol.term_structure`. Check fixed levels first: front_inverted, inverted, flat. Then compared with the last sessions, is near-term fear flatter than usual, usual, or steeper?

criteria.front_inverted: nine-day VIX at or above VIX
criteria.inverted: VIX at or above three-month VIX
criteria.flat: VIX at or over the near-flat line but under three-month VIX
criteria.flatter_than_usual: ratio in the top fifth of recent reads, not flat
criteria.usual: between the top and bottom fifths of recent reads
criteria.steeper_than_usual: ratio in the bottom fifth of recent reads

vol_curve_vs_usual.why: A day-level regime read: pure ranks go blind after about 20 stressed sessions, so fixed levels come first; the nine-day inversion is the one inversion that actually happened.

stress_state.cadence: every 30-minute read, awake only while the stress label is written
stress_state.ask: What kind of selloff is this stress day?
stress_state.instructions: Read `vol.stress_path`. The label is written only on stress days. Check in order: liquidation, exhaustion, bounce_not_believed, orderly_decline. Is the selloff a liquidation, exhausting, a bounce the fear gauge does not believe, or orderly?

criteria.orderly_decline: none of the above: price lower with VIX rising roughly in line
criteria.liquidation: price at or near the session low, VIX at new session highs, TICK repeatedly at its selling extreme
criteria.exhaustion: VIX has given back a good share of its rise from the session high while SPX holds above its low
criteria.bounce_not_believed: price has bounced off its low but VIX has not come down

code_criteria.liquidation: within {near_low_sigma} of the low, VIX at its session high, {tick_cluster} or more readings at -{tick_extreme} in {window_30_min} minutes
code_criteria.exhaustion: VIX retreat share >= {stress_retreat_share} and price >= {bounce_sigma} off the low
code_criteria.bounce_not_believed: price >= {bounce_sigma} off the low, retreat share < {stress_hold_share}

stress_state.why: Selloff days are where intraday momentum is strongest and where a VIX retreat off the high is the classic turn; none of the 59 calm sessions reaches this state for long, so the question sleeps until it matters.

groups.purpose: The same-day book in neutral words: whether the books agree, distance to the gamma flip, the move crossed with the book, the book's calm after the late morning, the cushion and where the gamma sits in both books.

book_balance_agreement.ask: Which way do today's same-day options books lean at the current price?
book_balance_agreement.instructions: Read `gex.book_balance` and `gex.balance_vs_yesterday`. Which describes today's same-day options book at the current price? Check in order: balanced, the two split options, tipped_overnight, then the agreed options.

criteria.balanced: at least one book is too close to call
criteria.split_oi_puts_vol_calls: the open-interest book leans to puts while today's volume book leans to calls
criteria.split_oi_calls_vol_puts: the open-interest book leans to calls while today's volume book leans to puts
criteria.tipped_overnight: both books agree, but on the other side from yesterday's close
criteria.calls_heavier_both: call gamma outweighs put gamma at price in both books, same side as yesterday's close
criteria.puts_heavier_both: put gamma outweighs call gamma at price in both books, same side as yesterday's close

code_criteria.tipped_overnight: agree and differ from the prior day's last RTH regime

book_balance_agreement.why: Replaces gamma_sign_trust with words that describe what code computed (the call-vs-put gamma balance at price), so JEV's 'long gamma pins' prior never fires; split books are where reversion to VWAP and of the 30-minute move is measurable, and the two split directions are not symmetric.

flip_distance_lean.ask: How far is price from the gamma flip?
flip_distance_lean.instructions: Read `gex.flip_distance`. Do not say which side of the flip price is on. Check no_flip first, then crossed_recently, then the distance. How far is price from the gamma flip?

criteria.no_flip: no flip was found or the book is balanced
criteria.crossed_recently: price crossed the flip within the last half hour
criteria.near_flip: price is within the far line of the flip
criteria.far_from_flip: price is more than the far line from the flip

code_criteria.no_flip: flip null or regime uncertain (checked first)
code_criteria.crossed_recently: sign changed vs the row {window_30_min} minutes earlier (checked second)

flip_distance_lean.why: In this data the sign is price's side of the flip, and the distance carries the direction lean the plain long/short word flattens; asking the distance removes the textbook damping prior. The deferred flip_position_cross becomes an option (crosses are rare because the flip travels with price).

rise_above_flip.ask: Did price move, and which way do the options books lean?
rise_above_flip.instructions: Read `price.recent_move` and `gex.book_balance`. Do not say which way price went. Did price move past the move rule, and which way do the books lean? The criteria assume neither continuation nor reversal; code learns the mapping.

criteria.moved_calls_heavier: price moved more than the move rule and both books lean to calls
criteria.moved_puts_heavier: price moved more than the move rule and both books lean to puts
criteria.moved_books_split: price moved more than the move rule and the books disagree or one is balanced
criteria.no_move: price stayed within the move rule

rise_above_flip.why: The single cross of the move with the book. It repeats much of the move (NMI 0.865), but the one cell that separates is measurable, and the split cells now carry a side because under split books the move reverses.

book_vs_pace.cadence: every 30-minute read from 11:32 (asleep before the late-morning gate)
book_vs_pace.ask: How does the options book's balance pair with the pace?
book_vs_pace.instructions: Read `gex.book_balance` and `vol.realized_vs_clock_rank`. The label's hot-line words decide the pace. Which pairing is it?

criteria.calls_heavier_normal: both books lean to calls and the last half hour moved at a normal or slow pace for its clock
criteria.calls_heavier_hot: both lean to calls and the last half hour moved faster than the hot line
criteria.puts_heavier_hot: both lean to puts and the last half hour moved faster than the hot line
criteria.puts_heavier_normal: both lean to puts at a normal or slow pace
criteria.split: the books disagree or one is balanced

code_criteria.calls_heavier_normal: both long, last half-hour realized over its same-clock median <= {rv_hot}

book_vs_pace.why: The book's calming effect exists only after the opening hours; asking it all day blurred it into nothing, which made the sign look inverted. The pace input is now the last half hour, not the whole day's pace.

gamma_cushion.ask: How much room does the book's balance have before it tips?
gamma_cushion.instructions: Read `gex.cushion_if_moved`. Check puts_heavier_now first. Which describes how much room the book's balance has before it tips?

criteria.puts_heavier_now: put gamma already outweighs call gamma at price
criteria.sturdy: a move either way leaves the book call-heavy with room to spare
criteria.thin_below: a drop leaves it call-heavy but under the thin line; a rise holds
criteria.tips_below: a drop would tip the balance to puts; a rise holds
criteria.soft_above: a rise would thin or tip the balance; a drop holds
criteria.soft_both: moves either way thin or tip the balance

code_criteria.sturdy: both sides keep >= {cushion_thin} of today's level

gamma_cushion.why: It serves size, not direction: when only a drop would tip the book the next hour ran wider, with no direction lean. Worded as the balance tipping, not dealers flipping.

gamma_weight_both_books.ask: Where does the gamma sit in today's book and the week's?
gamma_weight_both_books.instructions: Read `gex.weight_both_books`. The label's even-band words decide. Where does the gamma sit in today's same-day book and in the 1-to-7-day book (today's expiry excluded)?

criteria.both_below: both books sit past the even band below price
criteria.both_above: both books sit past the even band above price
criteria.week_below_today_not: the 1-to-7-day book sits past the even band below price; today's book is inside the band or above
criteria.week_above_today_not: the 1-to-7-day book sits past the even band above price; today's book is inside the band or below
criteria.week_even: the 1-to-7-day book is inside the even band

gamma_weight_both_books.why: Before noon today's same-day book holds about a third of the gamma dealers hedge; the week's book fires on more days and disagrees with today's on a third of reads. No 'lid or floor' wording: the two old texts contradicted each other.

groups.purpose: The book's structure against price: magnet seat, wall box, wall motion, wall touches, strike defense, and VWAP stretch crossed with book agreement.

magnet_seat.ask: Is price seated on today's heaviest strike, near it, or away?

criteria.held_on_magnet: price sits within the seat distance of the heaviest strike, has spent past the hug share of the last half hour there, it is the same strike, and its grip is above the median for this time of day
criteria.seated_fresh: within the seat distance now, but only recently, or the strike just changed, or the grip is ordinary
criteria.near: the heaviest strike is between the seat distance and the near distance away
criteria.away: the heaviest strike is beyond the near distance

code_criteria.held_on_magnet: distance < {magnet_seat_sigma}, time near >= {pin_hug_hi} of the window, same strike, grip rank >= {half_rank}

magnet_seat.why: The one tradeability signal that beats the clock on SPX: a seated, gripping pin means a flatter next half hour. It is a speed limit, not a magnet, until the last half hour (see settle_pull_side). Grip is ranked at the same clock because it climbs all day.

wall_box.ask: How tight is the box between the heaviest call-side and put-side strikes?
wall_box.instructions: Read `gex.wall_box` and `gex.walls_since_30min`. Which describes the box between the heaviest call-side and put-side strikes?

criteria.tight_standing: the two heavy strikes are under the tight width apart and unchanged for the last half hour
criteria.tight_redrawing: under the tight width apart, but a heavy strike just changed
criteria.middling: between the tight and wide widths apart
criteria.wide: more than the wide width apart

wall_box.why: A tight standing box is a quiet read; the morning/later split re-asked the clock that code already blends, so it is gone.

walls_motion.ask: How did the heaviest strikes move over the last {window_30_min} minutes?
walls_motion.instructions: Read `gex.walls_since_30min`. Check both_moved_up and both_moved_down first. Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, how did the heaviest call-side and put-side strikes move?

criteria.both_moved_up: both heavy strikes are now at higher strikes
criteria.both_moved_down: both heavy strikes are now at lower strikes
criteria.pulled_in: the two heavy strikes are closer together
criteria.spread_out: the two heavy strikes are further apart
criteria.stood_still: both heavy strikes are where they were

code_criteria.pulled_in: call down or put up, gap narrower

walls_motion.why: Keeps the one part of walls_vs_move that changes within the day and drops the repeat of the move (77% of its answers were no_move); code crosses it with the move.

wall_touch_effort.cadence: every 30-minute read, awake only when a wall or the magnet was touched in the last half hour
wall_touch_effort.ask: What happened at the heavy strike price touched?
wall_touch_effort.instructions: Read `levels.wall_touch_effort`. Check the break and hold options first. What happened at the heavy strike price touched?

criteria.broke_through_call_side: price went through the call-side heavy strike above and stayed through
criteria.broke_through_put_side: price went through the put-side heavy strike below and stayed through
criteria.held_at_call_side: price tested the call-side heavy strike and pulled back down
criteria.held_at_put_side: price tested the put-side heavy strike and pulled back up
criteria.touching_heavy_effort: touching now with SPY volume in the top band for these minutes
criteria.touching_light_effort: touching now with SPY volume in the middle or bottom band

code_criteria.broke_through_call_side: closed beyond by > {wall_touch_sigma} and still beyond

wall_touch_effort.why: Signed options so the loop learns direction; no_touch (78% of reads) is removed by gating, so the default answer never enters the weights.

strike_defense.cadence: every 30-minute read, awake only when a contested strike is within the defense distance
strike_defense.ask: Are market makers defending the nearest heavily hit strike or leaving it?
strike_defense.instructions: Read `options.strike_defense`. At the nearest strike within reach where same-day quotes keep getting hit, are market makers putting quotes back or leaving them empty, and is it above or below price?

criteria.defended_above: contested strike above price, refilled on at least the refill share of hits
criteria.abandoned_above: contested strike above price, refilled on less than the refill share
criteria.defended_below: contested strike below price, refilled on at least the refill share
criteria.abandoned_below: contested strike below price, refilled on less than the refill share

strike_defense.why: The only order-book read with any support here; it reads the options book's refill, not SPY's top of book.

vwap_side_vs_books.ask: Which side of the day's average price is SPX, and do the books agree?
vwap_side_vs_books.instructions: Read `price.vs_vwap` and `gex.book_balance`. The opening words of each label decide. Check near_average first. Which situation is it?

criteria.near_average: price is within the move rule of the day's average price
criteria.above_books_agree: price is above the day's average by more than the move rule, and both books lean the same way
criteria.above_books_split: above by more than the move rule, and the books disagree or one is balanced
criteria.below_books_agree: below by more than the move rule, and both books lean the same way
criteria.below_books_split: below by more than the move rule, and the books disagree or one is balanced

code_criteria.above_books_agree: > {move_rule_sigma} above, regime == volume book, neither uncertain

vwap_side_vs_books.why: Every option carries a side. Whether a departure from the average comes back depends on the books agreeing, not on the long/short word, which just repeats which side of the flip price is on. The stretch size and minutes since the last touch ride in the label.

groups.purpose: Where price sits against yesterday's value area and range, round levels, armed breaks, the overnight range, and heavy trading that is not moving price.

prior_value_location.ask: Where is price against yesterday's value area, and which way is today going?
prior_value_location.instructions: Read `levels.prior_value` for where price sits against the band where SPX spent most of yesterday's session, and `price.day_move` for which way today has gone since the settled open. Pick the option that matches both.

criteria.below_value_rallying: price is below yesterday's value band even though today is up or flat
criteria.below_value_falling: price is below yesterday's value band and today is down
criteria.above_value_rising: price is above yesterday's value band and today is up or flat
criteria.above_value_slipping: price is above yesterday's value band but today is down
criteria.inside_value: price is inside, or within the edge distance of, yesterday's value band

code_criteria.below_value_rallying: more than {value_edge_sigma} below the value-area low, day move from the open >= -{move_rule_sigma}
code_criteria.above_value_rising: more than {value_edge_sigma} above the high, day move >= -{move_rule_sigma}
code_criteria.inside_value: inside, or within {value_edge_sigma} of, the band

prior_value_location.why: Traders judge acceptance against yesterday's fair value. Today's move alone predicts nothing here, but a rally that stays below yesterday's value tends to fail and strength above value tends to keep going. Round 1 used only yesterday's high and low.

prior_day_acceptance.ask: What is price doing at yesterday's high or low?
prior_day_acceptance.instructions: Read `levels.prior_day`. Where price is now decides first. Check in order: rejected_back_inside, accepted_beyond, testing_edge, inside_away. Which situation is it at yesterday's high or low?

criteria.rejected_back_inside: price poked beyond yesterday's high or low and is now back inside
criteria.accepted_beyond: price is beyond yesterday's high or low now and has been beyond it for at least the acceptance time
criteria.testing_edge: price is within reach of yesterday's high or low, or beyond it for less than the acceptance time
criteria.inside_away: inside yesterday's range, away from both edges

code_criteria.testing_edge: within {level_reach_sigma} of an edge, or beyond for < {accept_minutes} minutes

prior_day_acceptance.why: Folded: the high and low mirrors share one table with direction learned relative to the edge's side (named in the label), and the location-first wording avoids the SNDK back-inside misread.

round_level_cross.cadence: every 30-minute read and every 5-minute lane read, awake only near or just through a round level
round_level_cross.ask: Has price just crossed a round level, or is it pressing one?
round_level_cross.instructions: Read `levels.round_number`. Has price just pushed through a round level, or is it pressing one without crossing?

criteria.just_crossed_up: within the cross window price rose through a round level and is still above it
criteria.just_crossed_down: within the cross window price fell through a round level and is still below it
criteria.pressing_from_below: price is just under a round level it has not crossed
criteria.pressing_from_above: price is just over a round level it has not broken

code_criteria.just_crossed_up: level inside a bar's range within {cross_lookback_min} min, price {round_near_sigma}+ below it before, above now

round_level_cross.why: Almost every SPX trader marks the big round numbers; order data shows stops cluster just past them and speed the move once crossed. The levels are also the big SPXW strikes, so it goes on the overlap list with the wall questions.

break_armed.cadence: every 30-minute read from 10:02, awake only while a break is armed or recently expired
break_armed.sleep_when: break_state idle and nothing expired or decocked within {window_30_min} minutes
break_armed.ask: Is a level-break setup armed, and which way?
break_armed.instructions: Read `levels.break_armed`. Is a level-break setup armed right now, and which way? The opening words decide.

criteria.armed_up: a break upward through a nearby level is armed and has not fired or expired
criteria.armed_down: a break downward through a nearby level is armed and has not fired or expired
criteria.recently_expired: an armed break expired or was called off within the last half hour

break_armed.why: The station arms this setup only when the book leans to puts and price was just turned back at a named level; its direction comes from the level, not the last move, and it survives a momentum control. It is the usable part of level_reclaim, which never fired.

overnight_range_position.ask: Where is price against the overnight futures range?
overnight_range_position.instructions: Read `overnight.range` and `overnight.price_vs_range`. Where price is now decides first. Check in order: above, below, the two back-inside options, near an edge, middle.

criteria.above_overnight_high: now more than the break distance above the overnight high
criteria.below_overnight_low: now more than the break distance below the overnight low
criteria.inside_now_after_breaking_above: inside the overnight range now after trading above its high earlier today (the open counts)
criteria.inside_now_after_breaking_below: inside now after trading below its low earlier today
criteria.inside_near_edge: no break today, inside or within the break distance of an overnight edge, within the near distance
criteria.inside_middle: no break today, away from both edges

code_criteria.inside_near_edge: inside or up to {on_break_sigma} beyond, within {on_near_sigma} of an edge

overnight_range_position.why: Futures traders watch the overnight edges; one question with one buffer instead of two, and the open location becomes the earlier-break history. Needs the new /ESZ26 overnight save job.

activity_vs_move.ask: Did option or SPY activity come with a price move?
activity_vs_move.instructions: Read `options.premium_pace_30`, `volume.spy_pace_30` and `price.recent_move`. Use the premium label; use SPY volume only when the premium label is absent. Which pairing is it?

criteria.heavy_no_move: trading in the top fifth for this time of day while price moved less than the move rule
criteria.heavy_with_move: trading in the top fifth and price moved more than the move rule
criteria.light: trading in the bottom fifth, whatever price did

activity_vs_move.why: Heavy trading that is not moving price is absorption; unproven, so it stays live and goes on the overlap list with realized_vs_clock.

groups.purpose: NYSE and S&P-member breadth: agreement with the move (sign-free), the day's breadth regime, TICK against its usual, unconfirmed extremes (with IWM) and members vs price and vs NYSE.

breadth_agrees_with_move.ask: Does breadth side with the last half hour's move?
breadth_agrees_with_move.instructions: Read `price.recent_move` and `breadth.upvol_share_30m`. Do not say which way price went; say only whether breadth sides with the move. Which describes it?

criteria.agrees_with_move: price moved more than the move rule, and the up-volume share leans the same way past its line
criteria.against_move: price moved more than the move rule, and the up-volume share leans the opposite way past its line
criteria.move_without_breadth: price moved more than the move rule, and the up-volume share sits in its even band
criteria.breadth_leans_price_still: price stayed inside the move rule, but the up-volume share leans past a line either way

code_criteria.agrees_with_move: |move| > {move_rule_sigma}, share past {upvol_lean_hi} or {upvol_lean_lo} on the move's side

breadth_agrees_with_move.why: Template for every 'X vs the move' cross: sign-free options leave direction to price_move_5way alone, so the combiner does not count the move again inside each cross (SNDK closes_agree was retired for exactly this). Code multiplies agree/against by the move's sign.

breadth_day_regime.ask: Since the open, has volume been lopsided, rotating or leaning?
breadth_day_regime.instructions: Read `breadth.day_upvol_share`. Apply in order and take the first that fits. Since the open, has volume been lopsided, faded from lopsided, rotating, or leaning?

criteria.one_sided_up: at least the one-sided share of today's volume went into rising stocks without rotation
criteria.one_sided_down: at least the one-sided share went into falling stocks without rotation
criteria.faded_from_one_side: lopsided earlier today, now back near even
criteria.rotational: the share keeps crossing even: a range day
criteria.leaning: tilts one way but not strongly or steadily

code_criteria.faded_from_one_side: was past, now within the even band

breadth_day_regime.why: A rotating-day read for the flat bucket; unproven, so live.

tick_lean_vs_usual.ask: Did the NYSE tick lean to buying or selling more than usual for this half hour?
tick_lean_vs_usual.instructions: Read `breadth.tick_side_vs_usual`. Compared with a usual half hour at this time of day, did the NYSE tick sit above zero more often, less often, or about as usual?
criteria: the share above zero was more than the far band below usual
between the usual and far bands below usual
within the usual band
between the usual and far bands above usual
more than the far band above usual
tick_lean_vs_usual.why: Two questions counted the same TICK side, and raw TICK sits below zero most of the time (median share above zero 0.33), so both answered 'selling' in a rising market. One question, measured against the usual for the clock.

new_extreme_unconfirmed.cadence: every 30-minute read, awake only when SPX set a new session extreme within the recent window
new_extreme_unconfirmed.ask: Did breadth confirm SPX's new session extreme?
new_extreme_unconfirmed.instructions: Read `price.session_extreme_recent` and `breadth.at_extremes`. SPX just set a new session high or low; do not say which. Did NYSE net volume reach its level at the previous extreme, and are small caps within the confirm rule of their own extreme?

criteria.extreme_confirmed: NYSE net volume reached its level at the previous extreme, and small caps (IWM) are within the confirm rule of their own extreme
criteria.extreme_unconfirmed: NYSE net volume fell short of its level at the previous extreme, or small caps are beyond the confirm rule from their own extreme

code_criteria.extreme_confirmed: VOLD at or past its level at the previous extreme and IWM within {smallcap_confirm_sigma} of its own extreme

new_extreme_unconfirmed.why: The classic narrow-push tell. The megacap basket almost never splits (QQQ confirmed 97 of 101 SPX highs), while small caps split about in half, so IWM replaces it; no_new_extreme is removed by gating.

member_breadth_vs_price_day.ask: Is SPX's move since the open backed by net buying in its own stocks?
member_breadth_vs_price_day.instructions: Read `price.day_move` and `breadth.members_net_day`. Is SPX's move since the open backed by net buying volume in S&P 500 stocks, or does that volume point the other way?

criteria.up_backed: SPX is past the open-day line above the settled open and S&P 500 net volume is positive
criteria.up_unbacked: SPX is past the open-day line above the open but S&P 500 net volume is zero or negative
criteria.down_backed: SPX is past the open-day line below the open and net volume is negative
criteria.down_unbacked: SPX is past the open-day line below the open but net volume is zero or positive
criteria.near_open: SPX is within the open-day line of the settled open

code_criteria.up_backed: day move > {open_day_move_sigma}, members' net volume positive
code_criteria.up_unbacked: day move > {open_day_move_sigma}, members' net volume zero or negative

member_breadth_vs_price_day.why: A day move made on the members' own net selling is carried by a few heavy names or futures, and it stalled or turned more often. $VOLSPD is S&P 500 up-minus-down volume, not Nasdaq breadth as round 1 and the feed probe said.

member_vs_nyse_breadth.ask: Has net volume in S&P 500 stocks been stronger or weaker than across the NYSE?
member_vs_nyse_breadth.instructions: Read `breadth.members_net_day`. The label's split-line words decide. Since the open, compared with usual for this time of day, has net volume in S&P 500 stocks been stronger, weaker, or matched against all NYSE stocks?

criteria.members_stronger: S&P 500 net volume is stronger than NYSE-wide net volume by more than the split line
criteria.members_weaker: weaker by more than the split line

member_vs_nyse_breadth.why: The two tallies usually agree (0.91); when the index's own members lag the whole exchange, big-cap selling is hidden by ADRs, funds and smaller listings.

breadth_flip_after_release.cadence: every 30-minute read, awake only within the digest window after an in-session release
breadth_flip_after_release.ask: Since the release, has NYSE volume switched sides?
breadth_flip_after_release.instructions: Read `breadth.flip_after_release`. Since this session's release, has the share of NYSE volume in rising stocks switched sides against the hour before it?

criteria.flipped_to_buying: past the low line before the release, past the high line since
criteria.flipped_to_selling: past the high line before the release, past the low line since
criteria.kept_side: past the same line before and since the release
criteria.no_clear_side: inside the even band before or since the release

code_criteria.kept_side: same side past its line both times

breadth_flip_after_release.why: A release that flips which stocks carry the volume has changed the day's story; one that leaves the breadth side alone was noise.

volume_vs_count.ask: Did volume run heavier in rising or falling stocks than their count suggests?
volume_vs_count.instructions: Read `breadth.volume_vs_count_30m`. Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, did volume run heavier in rising stocks than their count would suggest, heavier in falling stocks, or matched?

criteria.volume_ahead_rising: volume per rising stock ran heavier than volume per falling stock, past the low line
criteria.volume_ahead_falling: volume per falling stock ran heavier, past the high line

volume_vs_count.why: TRIN's information that up-volume share and the advance count each miss: whether the money is concentrated on one side.

groups.purpose: Who carries the index: equal weight (beta-adjusted), semis, sectors, the megacaps' cohesion, top-8 vs the rest, and QQQ vs IWM over the day.

move_breadth.ask: Did the typical stock move with the index, or did the biggest stocks carry it?
move_breadth.instructions: Read `price.recent_move` and `leaders.equal_weight_vs_cap_30m`. Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, after allowing for equal weight's usual swing, did the typical stock move with the index, or did the biggest stocks carry it?

criteria.broad: the index moved past the move rule and the typical stock moved about as much or more, the same way
criteria.narrow: the index moved but the typical stock lagged by more than the split rule
criteria.hidden_move: the index stayed inside the move rule but the typical stock moved past the split rule

code_criteria.broad: |move| > {move_rule_sigma}, residual not against the move by more than {eqw_split_sigma}
code_criteria.narrow: |move| > {move_rule_sigma}, residual against the move by more than {eqw_split_sigma}
