move_breadth.why: Beta-adjusted: raw RSP moves only 0.66x SPY, so the raw gap made every big move look narrow. Sign-free so the move is not counted twice.

semis_tell.ask: Did semiconductors run ahead of the index, and which way?
semis_tell.instructions: Read `leaders.semis_vs_index_30m` and `price.recent_move`. After allowing for chips usually moving further than the index, did semis run ahead upward, ahead downward, in line, or stay quiet?

criteria.ahead_up: chips beat their usual multiple of the index by more than the lead rule
criteria.ahead_down: chips trailed their usual multiple by more than the lead rule
criteria.in_line: the index moved and chips moved about their usual multiple
criteria.quiet: the index did not move and chips did nothing beyond their usual multiple

semis_tell.why: Chips lead the AI-weighted index; the side is in the option, not a product with the move.

sector_agreement.ask: Did the sector funds move together with the index?
sector_agreement.instructions: Read `sectors.agreement_30m` and `price.recent_move`. Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, did the sector funds move together with the index, only partly, or swap places under a flat index?

criteria.one_way: the index moved and at least {sector_one_way} of {sector_count} sectors moved with it
criteria.patchy_move: the index moved but fewer sectors went along
criteria.rotation_under_flat: the index barely moved but sectors moved hard in opposite directions
criteria.quiet: the index barely moved and sectors were quiet

sector_agreement.why: Index variance is component variance times correlation; rotation under a flat index is the best-grounded chop idea outside price.

megacap_cohesion.ask: How did the largest index stocks move together over the last {window_30_min} minutes?
megacap_cohesion.instructions: Read `leaders.megacap_cohesion_30m`. Check in order: one_name, together_up, together_down, cancelling, drifting. How did the largest index stocks move over the last {window_30_min} minutes?

criteria.one_name: one big stock supplied more than the one-name share of a real index move
criteria.together_up: at least {mega_together} of the {mega_count} largest rose together
criteria.together_down: at least {mega_together} of the {mega_count} largest fell together
criteria.cancelling: giants moved hard both ways, cancelling
criteria.drifting: the giants were mostly quiet or patternless

code_criteria.cancelling: two or more up and two or more down past their rule

megacap_cohesion.why: Concentration flag. one_name almost never fired at the old rule (1.5% of windows); the basket now comes from weights, with TSLA in and Alphabet's two share classes combined.

leaders_vs_rest.ask: Which part of the index did the moving over the last {window_30_min} minutes?
leaders_vs_rest.instructions: Read `leaders.pull_vs_rest_30m`. Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, which part of the index did the moving: the largest names, the rest, both the same way, or the two pulling against each other?

criteria.leaders_carry_up: the largest names pushed the index up past the pull rule and the rest stayed inside it
criteria.leaders_carry_down: the largest names pushed it down past the pull rule and the rest stayed inside it
criteria.rest_carries: the rest moved past the pull rule while the largest names stayed inside it
criteria.together: both parts moved past the pull rule the same way
criteria.tug_of_war: both parts moved past the pull rule in opposite directions
criteria.quiet: neither part moved past the pull rule

leaders_vs_rest.why: Cap-weighted split: is one group the index today. A tug of war under a pinned index is megacap_pull_at_pin's case, now crossed by code with magnet_seat instead of a pin-gated question that was not_pinned on over 95% of reads.

size_leadership_day.cadence: every 30-minute read from 10:32 (signal measured from 12:00; asked earlier so the weights learn the morning is weak)
size_leadership_day.ask: Since the open, have tech or small caps led the index?
size_leadership_day.instructions: Read `leaders.size_spread_day`. Since the settled open, after allowing for each fund's usual swing against SPY, which group has led: the Nasdaq-100 fund QQQ, the small-cap fund IWM, both, or neither?

criteria.tech_led: QQQ is ahead of IWM by more than the leadership rule and ahead of its usual swing
criteria.small_led: IWM is ahead of QQQ by more than the leadership rule and ahead of its usual swing
criteria.both_ahead: both are ahead of their usual swing and close to each other
criteria.both_behind: both are behind their usual swing and close to each other

size_leadership_day.why: Leadership only shows over hours; the 30-minute version carries nothing and repeats move_breadth, so this is deliberately day-long. The label says who led and code learns the sign (textbook reads small-cap leadership as risk-on; this tape did the opposite).

groups.purpose: Outside markets ahead of the index (bonds, oil, the pooled macro complex, sector risk rotation) and the calendar (expiry cycle, month turn).

bond_catchup.ask: Are Treasuries ahead of the index, and which way?
bond_catchup.instructions: Read `xasset.bond_gap_30min`. Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, are Treasuries ahead of the index in the direction that has gone with stocks rising this hour, ahead in the stocks-falling direction, in line, or is the link too loose to say?

criteria.bonds_ahead_up: bonds moved further than the index's move would match, in the direction that has gone with stocks rising this hour, and the link is tight
criteria.bonds_ahead_down: bonds moved further than the index's move would match, in the direction that has gone with stocks falling, and the link is tight
criteria.in_line: bonds and the index moved by matching amounts under this hour's link
criteria.link_loose: bonds and stocks barely moved together this hour, or the bond market is closed

code_criteria.bonds_ahead_up: gap rank >= {top_fifth} in the stocks-up direction and link >= {bond_link_tight}

bond_catchup.why: When Treasury prices run ahead of what the index's move would match and the two have been trading together, the index tends to follow; the label states today's link sign, so it works in either stock-bond regime. $TNX bars stop at 15:00, so TLT or /ZN is the source.

oil_gap.ask: Did oil move further than its usual link to the index explains?
oil_gap.instructions: Read `xasset.oil_gap_30min`. Over the last {window_30_min} minutes, did oil move further than its usual link to the index would explain, and which way?

criteria.oil_ran_up: oil rose more than the index's move usually brings, top fifth for this half hour
criteria.oil_ran_down: oil fell more than the index's move usually brings, bottom fifth
criteria.in_line: an ordinary amount given the index

oil_gap.why: Oil has moved against stocks in this tape; an oil jump the index has not absorbed has come before weakness. Code learns the sign; the label never says bullish or bearish.

macro_lean.ask: Are bonds, credit, oil, gold and the euro ahead of the index, and which way?
macro_lean.instructions: Read `xasset.macro_gap_30min` and `price.recent_move`. Taken together, are bonds, high-yield credit, oil, gold and the euro ahead of the index in the stocks-up direction, ahead in the stocks-down direction, or in line?

criteria.complex_ahead_up: the outside markets together moved further toward stocks-up than the index did, top fifth
criteria.in_line: the outside markets and the index agree in size

macro_lean.why: One pooled read catches macro repricing the index has not joined yet, without near-duplicate single-asset questions. It replaces cross_asset_confirm, whose UUP feed is broken and whose risk-off signs are wrong in this tape, and absorbs gold.

risk_rotation.ask: Did risk-on sectors beat or trail the defensive ones?
risk_rotation.instructions: Read `leaders.rotation_30m`. After allowing for each sector's usual link to the index, did financials, discretionary and industrials beat utilities, staples and health care, trail them, or neither?

criteria.risk_on: the sensitive sectors beat the defensives by more than the rotation rule
criteria.risk_off: the defensives beat the sensitive sectors by more than the rotation rule
criteria.level: within the rule of each other

risk_rotation.why: Sector risk appetite beneath the index; unproven, live.

expiry_calendar.ask: Which part of the expiry cycle is today?
expiry_calendar.instructions: Read `calendar.expiry_phase`. Check in order: quarter_end, monthly_or_quarterly, opex_week, week_after_opex, ordinary. Which part of the expiry cycle is today?

criteria.quarter_end: the quarter's last trading day: the quarter-end SPXW book settles at today's close
criteria.monthly_or_quarterly: monthly or quarterly expiry: the morning-settled monthly book settled on the opening prints and daily SPXW settle at the close
criteria.opex_week: inside the opex-week window before this month's monthly expiry
criteria.week_after_opex: one of the trading days after a monthly expiry

expiry_calendar.why: SPX lists an expiry every day, but the monthly is morning-settled (its gamma is gone after Friday's open) while the quarter-end book is close-settled. Split out of calendar_flow_day so the one-window rule no longer hides 09-30.

month_turn_flow.ask: Which month-turn flow is in play for the rest of today?
month_turn_flow.instructions: Read `calendar.month_turn` and `flows.rebalance_side`. Which month-turn flow is in play for the rest of today?

criteria.last_days_stocks_overweight: one of the month's last sessions after stocks beat bonds by a top-fifth margin: funds expected to sell stocks, mostly into the close
criteria.last_days_stocks_underweight: one of the last sessions after stocks lagged bonds by a bottom-fifth margin: funds expected to buy stocks into the close
criteria.last_days_small_gap: one of the last sessions with an ordinary stock-bond gap
criteria.first_days_of_month: one of the first sessions of a new month, when new money is typically invested

code_criteria.last_days_stocks_overweight: trading days to month-end < {rebal_window_days} and the governing gap (named in the label) rank >= {top_fifth}

month_turn_flow.why: Turn of the month is the one calendar window with a local direction tilt; the rebalance side is worded as a close-and-next-day flow, which matches the published mechanism. It replaces calendar_flow_day's regime role and the sign lives in the options.

groups.purpose: The dark news feed seen through the tape: sudden bursts, whether they set extremes, the reaction path after any release or burst, vol's reaction, what moved with the shock, and single-name shocks.

shock_state.cadence: every 30-minute read and every 5-minute lane read
shock_state.sleep_when: no five-minute window in the last {shock_lookback_min} minutes with z >= {shock_z} and |move| >= {shock_floor_sigma}
shock_state.ask: What has price done since the last hour's shock?
shock_state.instructions: Read `shock.burst`. Price had a sudden burst in the last hour, far bigger than its recent minute-to-minute movement. What has happened since? Check in order: fresh, round_trip, settling.

criteria.fresh: a burst passed the shock rule and ended within the fresh window
criteria.round_trip: a burst older than the fresh window, and price has since given back more than the half line of it
criteria.settling: a burst older than the fresh window, and price has kept the half line or more of it

shock_state.why: News with no feed shows up as a burst far bigger than the tape's own recent wiggle; volatility clusters, so a fresh or round-tripped shock means a busier next half hour, even when the net move looks small. In the lane the burst is ranked against the same minute on recent sessions.

shock_at_extreme.cadence: every 30-minute read, awake only within an hour of a shock
shock_at_extreme.ask: Where did the shock take price against today's range?
shock_at_extreme.instructions: Read `shock.burst` and `shock.vs_day_range`. Where did the last hour's shock take price against today's range so far?

criteria.new_extreme_now: the shock set a new session high or low and price is still within the move rule of it
criteria.new_extreme_given_up: the shock set a new session high or low but price is now back beyond the move rule from it
criteria.inside_range: the shock stayed inside the day's earlier high and low

code_criteria.new_extreme_now: burst passed the prior session extreme; |spot - extreme| <= {move_rule_sigma}

shock_at_extreme.why: A burst that runs stops through the day's extreme with nothing behind it tends to snap back; a burst inside the range is more often real repricing. The side lives in the label.

move_reaction_path.cadence: every 30-minute read and lane read, awake 10-120 minutes after a release, Fed remarks, or a detected burst
move_reaction_path.sleep_when: the first reaction moved less than {event_reaction_rule} normal-day sigma
move_reaction_path.ask: What has price done since the first reaction to the latest release or burst?
move_reaction_path.instructions: Read `event.reaction`. What has price done since the first reaction to the latest release, Fed remarks or sudden burst? The label names which kind it was. Check extending first.

criteria.extending: price pushed past where the first reaction ended, the same way
criteria.holding: kept the half line or more of the first reaction without extending
criteria.faded: gave back more than the half line but has not crossed where the reaction started
criteria.reversed: crossed back through where the reaction started

code_criteria.faded: giveback > {gap_half_share}, same side of the start

move_reaction_path.why: Unscheduled headlines are SPX's largest move source and there is no feed, but the burst they leave is visible. Widening the trigger from the calendar to any burst lets the question fire about once a day and be graded; on Fed days the reaction starts at the press conference, where the real move came.

shock_vol_reaction.cadence: every 30-minute read, awake only within an hour of a shock
shock_vol_reaction.ask: Did VIX overreact or shrug at the shock?
shock_vol_reaction.instructions: Read `shock.burst` and `vol.vix_on_shock`. Since just before the shock, has VIX moved more than the price move alone explains, in line with it, or less? The opening words decide.

criteria.vol_overreacted: VIX moved more than the shock line beyond what the price move explains, in the fearful direction
criteria.in_line: VIX moved within the shock line of what the price move explains
criteria.vol_shrugged: VIX moved more than the shock line against what the price move explains

shock_vol_reaction.why: Whether options traders repriced risk is the best live proxy for 'was there a headline'; research expects repricing to mean drift, the station's small sample leans the other way, so the loop learns the sign.

shock_fingerprint.cadence: every 30-minute read, awake only within an hour of a shock
shock_fingerprint.instructions: Read `shock.burst` and `shock.cross_asset`. During the shock's five minutes, which group moved furthest beyond its usual link to the index? Pick the first that the labels say passed its rule.

criteria.rates_led: the ten-year yield moved more than its rule
criteria.tech_led: semiconductors moved more than their rule beyond the index
criteria.one_name: one megacap supplied more than its share rule of the burst
criteria.broad: most sector funds moved the shock's way and NYSE TICK hit an extreme the same way
criteria.defensive_bid: utilities, staples and health care rose against the index
criteria.no_fingerprint: nothing passed its rule: the shock was the index alone

shock_fingerprint.why: With no headline feed, what moved with the shock says what kind of news it was (rates or Fed headline, AI or chip news, macro shock hitting everything, single-company news, flight to safety); each kind resolves differently.

single_name_shock.cadence: every 30-minute read and lane read, awake only when a top-8 name passed the name-shock rule in the last 10 minutes
single_name_shock.ask: Did the big stock's shock stay alone or spread to other giants?
single_name_shock.instructions: Read `leaders.single_name_10m`. One of the largest index stocks just moved far past its usual move. Did it move alone, or did other giants join?

criteria.shock_up_alone: one heavy name jumped past the rule and the other large names stayed inside their usual moves
criteria.shock_down_alone: one heavy name dropped past the rule and the others stayed inside their usual moves
criteria.shock_up_spreading: one heavy name jumped past the rule and at least {spread_count} others rose past their usual move too
criteria.shock_down_spreading: one heavy name dropped past the rule and at least {spread_count} others fell past their usual move too

code_criteria.shock_up_alone: one name > +{name_shock_mult}x its same-clock median, fewer than {spread_count} others past their usual
code_criteria.shock_up_spreading: one name > +{name_shock_mult}x, {spread_count}+ others past their usual the same way

single_name_shock.why: Unscheduled single-name headlines (export rules, rulings, product news) move a stock before they move SPX; 'alone' is company news the index can digest, 'spreading' is a theme repricing.

groups.purpose: The 15:02 and 15:32 reads (from 14:02 for the settle pull): the afternoon leg the auction undoes, the settlement pull, the charm wall, late volume, and Fed press-conference afternoons.

afternoon_leg_into_close.horizon: 30min at the 15:32 read; 60min at the 15:02 read
afternoon_leg_into_close.cadence: the 15:02 and 15:32 reads only (weights keyed per read slot)
afternoon_leg_into_close.ask: Which way has price run since the early afternoon?
afternoon_leg_into_close.instructions: Read `price.afternoon_leg`. Which way has price run since the early-afternoon anchor the label names?

criteria.afternoon_up: price has risen more than the afternoon-leg rule
criteria.afternoon_down: price has fallen more than the afternoon-leg rule
criteria.afternoon_flat: price has stayed within the afternoon-leg rule

afternoon_leg_into_close.why: In the last half hour the closing auction undoes the afternoon's run; the 90-minute leg is the signal, not round 1's 30-minute leg or the day move. Earlier in the afternoon the same leg continues, so code learns a per-slot mapping. The day move from yesterday's close and the range position ride in the label (close_stretch merged: they add nothing once the leg is known).

settle_pull_side.cadence: the 14:02, 14:32, 15:02 and 15:32 reads (weights keyed per read slot: the pull shows only after 15:30)
settle_pull_side.sleep_when: magnet_seat's code answer is held_on_magnet or seated_fresh
settle_pull_side.ask: Where does today's heaviest strike sit against price before the settle?
settle_pull_side.instructions: Read `gex.settle_pull`. Check split first. Where does today's heaviest same-day strike sit against price, counted in what today's options still price before the settle?

criteria.magnet_above_in_reach: the magnet is above price, within the reach line of the move still priced
criteria.magnet_above_out_of_reach: the magnet is above price, beyond the reach line
criteria.magnet_below_in_reach: the magnet is below price, within the reach line
criteria.magnet_below_out_of_reach: the magnet is below price, beyond the reach line
criteria.split: the magnet and the gamma-weighted centre sit on opposite sides of price

code_criteria.split: magnet and pin_centroid more than {settle_seat_sigma} on opposite sides of price (checked first)

settle_pull_side.why: SPXW settles on the 16:00 print and dealer rehedging into settlement pulls the close toward the heavy strike, but locally only after 15:30 and through the 15:50 auction; the ruler for 'how far' shrinks all afternoon because today's options die at the close, so distance is counted in remaining straddles.

afternoon_charm_wall.ask: Where does the charm wall sit against price?
afternoon_charm_wall.instructions: Read `gex.charm_wall_distance`. Where does the charm wall sit compared with price?

criteria.charm_at_price: the charm wall is within the near-low distance of price
criteria.charm_above_near: between the near-low and near-high distances above price
criteria.charm_below_near: between the near-low and near-high distances below price

afternoon_charm_wall.why: Unproven, not disproven, so live on a 30-minute horizon (what the evidence measured); the charm sign never varies (negative on 50/50 days), so only the location is asked, with remaining straddles in the label.

late_volume_pace.ask: How heavy was trading in the last {window_30_min} minutes for this time of day?
late_volume_pace.instructions: Read `volume.spy_last30_share`. How heavy was trading in the last {window_30_min} minutes compared with the usual share for this time of day?

criteria.heavy: the last half hour carried more than the usual top-third share of today's volume

late_volume_pace.why: The closing auction is the day's biggest volume event; a heavy last half hour means programs are already working and the close moves further. It feeds P(flat) at the read where the clock baseline is weakest.

fed_presser_path.cadence: every 30-minute read after the press conference starts, FOMC days only (none in the test window; next 10-28)
fed_presser_path.ask: Since the Fed press conference began, has price extended or reversed the statement's move?
fed_presser_path.instructions: Read `event.statement_and_presser`. Check presser_flat, then presser_new_leg, then extends or reverses. Since the Fed chair's press conference began, has price gone with the statement's first move, against it, or nowhere?

criteria.presser_extends: since the press conference began price moved more than the presser rule the same way as the statement move
criteria.presser_reverses: moved more than the presser rule the other way
criteria.presser_new_leg: the statement barely moved price and the press conference has moved it more than the presser rule
criteria.presser_flat: the press conference has moved price less than the presser rule

fed_presser_path.why: On both FOMC days on disk the real move came during the press conference and lasted to the close; the statement's 15 minutes said little.

closing_window_vix.cadence: the 15:02 and 15:32 reads (weights keyed per read slot)
closing_window_vix.ask: Has VIX drifted up, held or drifted down since the early afternoon?
closing_window_vix.instructions: Read `vol.vix_since_1400`. Since the early-afternoon anchor the label names, has VIX drifted up, drifted down, or held, as a share of its level?

criteria.vix_drifting_up: VIX rose past the moving line
criteria.vix_held: VIX moved less than the moving line either way
criteria.vix_drifting_down: VIX fell past the moving line

closing_window_vix.why: Hedges bought or unwound into the close move VIX before the closing auction moves SPX; the afternoon drift is the one VIX read keyed to the close.

groups.purpose: Pre-market lane (all dark until the lane exists; the overnight store it reads is saved at 09:26), one 09:28 read: the overnight futures move in yesterday's sigma, the overnight session's width, and when the gap was made.

overnight_move_vs_expected.cadence: once at the 09:28 premarket read (premarket lane not built); answer held as a day constant through 10:30
overnight_move_vs_expected.ask: Which way and how far did futures move overnight?
overnight_move_vs_expected.instructions: Read `overnight.es_move`. Which way did futures move from yesterday's close to now, and how large was the move against the recent nights' moves to the same time?

criteria.big_down: futures fell, a move in the top third of the recent nights' moves
criteria.down: fell, a move in the middle third of the recent nights' moves
criteria.flat: moved either way, a move in the bottom third of the recent nights' moves
criteria.up: rose, a move in the middle third of the recent nights' moves
criteria.big_up: rose, a move in the top third of the recent nights' moves

code_criteria.big_down: move < 0 and |move| larger than over two thirds of the prior nights' |move| (top third)
code_criteria.down: move < 0 and |move| larger than a third to two thirds of them (middle third)
code_criteria.flat: |move| larger than under a third of them (bottom third)
code_criteria.up: move > 0 and |move| larger than a third to two thirds of them (middle third)
code_criteria.big_up: move > 0 and |move| larger than over two thirds of them (top third)

overnight_move_vs_expected.why: A signed pre-open read of the overnight vote: it leans slightly against the move for the first half hour and with it from 10:30; code learns both signs by clock bucket.

pm_overnight_session.cadence: once at the 09:28 premarket read (premarket lane not built); answer held as a day constant through 10:30
pm_overnight_session.ask: How wide was last night's futures session?
pm_overnight_session.instructions: Read `overnight.range_vs_normal`. How wide was last night's futures session compared with recent nights?

criteria.quiet_night: narrower than the quiet line times the recent median
criteria.normal_night: between the quiet and wide lines
criteria.wide_night: wider than the wide line times the recent median

pm_overnight_session.why: Volatility clusters overnight into the first hour, and futures pressing an edge at 09:28 set up an open outside the range: one read gives the 09:35 ten-minute call a size prior before any SPX bars exist.

gap_origin.cadence: once at the 09:28 premarket read (premarket lane not built); answer held as a day constant through 10:30
gap_origin.ask: When was most of the move from yesterday's close made?
gap_origin.instructions: Read `overnight.gap_origin`. When was most of the move from yesterday's close to now made?

criteria.no_gap: futures are within the gap rule of yesterday's close
criteria.made_at_data_release: more than the origin share of the gap came in the window after an early-morning report
criteria.made_overnight: more than the origin share drifted in overnight
criteria.made_in_last_hour: more than the origin share came in the last hour before the open
criteria.spread: no single window made more than the origin share

code_criteria.made_at_data_release: release window share > {origin_share} and a pre_open row today

gap_origin.why: Moved to premarket and asked once: a day constant asked all day repeats one answer. Its release branch could never fire until the calendar carried pre-open rows.

groups.purpose: Pre-market lane (built after Monday; dark until then), one 09:28 read: the 08:30 release's reaction path, and overnight bonds and bitcoin against the gap.

release_reaction_path.cadence: once at the 09:28 premarket read (premarket lane not built); answer held as a day constant through 10:30
release_reaction_path.ask: What did futures do after this morning's early report?
release_reaction_path.instructions: Read `overnight.release_reaction`. After this morning's early report, what did futures do between the first reaction and now? Check in order: shrugged, extended, faded, held.

criteria.shrugged: the first reaction was under the small-reaction line
criteria.extended: futures kept going the reaction's way by more than the half line of it
criteria.held: futures kept the half line or more of the reaction
criteria.faded: futures gave back more than the half line of the reaction

release_reaction_path.why: News at 08:30 is priced within a minute, so its direction is in the gap; what carries into the open is whether the market kept trading through it. The size of the reaction rides in the label for the size book.

overnight_bonds_vs_gap.cadence: once at the 09:28 premarket read (premarket lane not built); answer held as a day constant through 10:30
overnight_bonds_vs_gap.sleep_when: bonds and bitcoin in opposite outer thirds, or data missing
overnight_bonds_vs_gap.ask: Did Treasuries and bitcoin move further than today's gap overnight?
overnight_bonds_vs_gap.instructions: Read `overnight.bond_gap`. Since yesterday's close, did Treasuries and bitcoin move further toward stocks-up than today's gap, further toward stocks-down, or in line?

criteria.overnight_ahead_up: overnight bonds (with bitcoin not disagreeing) went further toward stocks-up than the gap did
criteria.overnight_ahead_down: overnight bonds went further toward stocks-down than the gap did
criteria.in_line: overnight bonds and the gap agree

overnight_bonds_vs_gap.why: Overnight bonds reprice on news before cash stocks open; a gap that bonds did not match tends to trade back toward the bonds' side in the first hour. Bitcoin, open all weekend, rides along as a Monday hint.

groups.purpose: Shadow only (proof they do not help): asked hourly, logged and graded, kept out of the weights.

flow_vs_price.shadow_proof: SPX aggressor tape, 20 and 46 days, worse than clock and shuffles
flow_vs_price.ask: Does the same-day options tape lean with the move or against it?
flow_vs_price.instructions: Read `price.recent_move` and `options.flow_lean_30`. Does the same-day options tape lean with the move, against it, or lean while price is still?

criteria.backs_move: price moved past the move rule and the flow leaned the same way past its line
criteria.fights_move: price moved past the move rule and the flow leaned the other way
criteria.lean_while_still: price within the move rule while the flow leaned one way
criteria.no_lean: the flow within its line of its usual level

code_criteria.backs_move: |move| > {move_rule_sigma}, lean past {flow_lean_rank} rank the same way

flow_vs_price.why: Kept only as a log: the options aggressor lean on SPX's own tape has already been shown not to help.

option_quote_liquidity.shadow_proof: partial corr 0.005 after past movement, 21 days
option_quote_liquidity.ask: Are same-day option quotes near price thinner or deeper than usual?
option_quote_liquidity.instructions: Read `options.quote_liquidity`. Are same-day option quotes near price thinner or wider than usual for this time of day?

criteria.thin_or_wide: depth in the bottom fifth or spread above its usual tick

code_criteria.thin_or_wide: depth rank <= {bottom_fifth} or spread above usual

option_quote_liquidity.why: Logged for completeness; measured, nothing there beyond past movement.

delta_weight_side.shadow_proof: residual -0.01 after spot; tracks price at -0.76
delta_weight_side.ask: Does dealers' directional exposure sit above or below price?
delta_weight_side.instructions: Read `gex.delta_weight_side`. Does most of dealers' directional exposure sit at strikes above price, below price, or evenly?

criteria.above: more than the high share above price
criteria.below: less than the low share above price

delta_weight_side.why: Built and unused by round 1; logged only, because it tracks where price sits in the day and adds nothing beyond price.

groups.purpose: Dark: the feed or data is missing on Monday; never asked. (Questions waiting only on a build stay dark in their home group.)

moc_imbalance_side.cadence: would need a 15:52 read with an 8-minute horizon (last live read is 15:32)
moc_imbalance_side.ask: Which side is the closing imbalance on, and is it large?
moc_imbalance_side.instructions: Read `close.moc_imbalance`. Which side is the published closing imbalance on, and is it large for today?

criteria.buy_large: a buy imbalance in the top fifth of recent closes
criteria.sell_large: a sell imbalance in the top fifth

moc_imbalance_side.why: 90% of the last 28 minutes' variance falls after 15:50, exactly the window this would see.

etf_flow_intraday.cadence: every 30-minute read when a feed exists
etf_flow_intraday.ask: Have index ETFs been created or redeemed heavily today?
etf_flow_intraday.instructions: Read `flows.etf_creations`. Since the open, have index ETFs been created or redeemed heavily for this time of day?
etf_flow_intraday.why: Intraday primary-market flow would show real money behind a move.

news_headline.cadence: on each new headline once a writer exists
news_headline.ask: What kind of market news just came out?
news_headline.instructions: Read `news.intraday_headline`. What kind of market news just came out, and is it new?

criteria.company_new: new single-company news in a large index stock
criteria.repeat: a repeat or rehash of known news

news_headline.why: Unscheduled headlines are SPX's largest move source; the price-only stand-ins are shock_state, shock_fingerprint and move_reaction_path.

nasdaq_breadth_lean.cadence: every 30-minute read when a feed exists
nasdaq_breadth_lean.ask: Did Nasdaq volume lean the same way as the NYSE?
nasdaq_breadth_lean.instructions: Read `breadth.nasdaq_net_volume`. Over the last half hour has Nasdaq volume leaned to rising or falling stocks, and does it agree with NYSE?

criteria.nasdaq_leads_up: Nasdaq up-volume share above the high line while NYSE is not
criteria.nasdaq_leads_down: Nasdaq share below the low line while NYSE is not

nasdaq_breadth_lean.why: Kept so the gap stays visible: $VOLSPD is S&P 500 breadth, not Nasdaq.

spy_book_lean.cadence: every 5-minute lane read and 30-minute read once persisted
spy_book_lean.ask: Has the pressure at SPY's best prices been on the buy or the sell side?
spy_book_lean.instructions: Read `liquidity.spy_book_lean`. Over the last five minutes, has the pressure at SPY's best prices been on the buy side, the sell side, or balanced?

criteria.buyers_pressing: order-flow imbalance at least the lean line above usual
criteria.sellers_pressing: at least the lean line below usual

spy_book_lean.why: Top-of-book order-flow imbalance is the best-documented short-horizon price driver; most likely to help the 10-minute call.

tomorrow_book_handoff.cadence: the 15:02 and 15:32 reads once a 1DTE slice is scanned
tomorrow_book_handoff.ask: Where does tomorrow's heaviest strike sit as today's options run out?
tomorrow_book_handoff.instructions: Read `expiry.next_book_magnet`. Check next_priced_big first. As today's options run out, where does tomorrow's heaviest strike sit, and is tomorrow priced as a normal day?

criteria.next_above_normal: tomorrow's heaviest strike is above price beyond the seat distance, usual pricing
criteria.next_below_normal: below price beyond the seat distance, usual pricing
criteria.next_at_price: within the seat distance of price, usual pricing
criteria.next_priced_big: tomorrow's straddle in the top fifth of recent sessions at this clock

tomorrow_book_handoff.why: Tests the 0DTE-to-1DTE hand-off, which SNDK never had.

quarter_end_collar_side.cadence: every 30-minute read on the quarter's last trading day (09-30, 12-31) once the band is kept
quarter_end_collar_side.ask: Where is price against today's largest quarter-end strikes?
quarter_end_collar_side.instructions: Read `expiry.quarter_end_strikes`. Where does price sit against the largest strikes of the quarter-end options expiring today?

criteria.near_short_call: within the collar distance below the largest call strike
criteria.near_long_put: within the collar distance above the largest put strike

quarter_end_collar_side.why: The largest single SPX options position (the hedged-equity collar) rolls on the quarter's last day; the station cannot see that book on its own today.
